defects.description: JSON.parse turns 64-bit ids into doubles, so ids above 2^53 lose their low bits and two consecutive upstream ids become equal, making dedupeById merge different records.
defects.why_missed: Suite ids are small integers that doubles represent exactly; the collapse is a property of the number range the upstream sequence reaches in production, never of a code branch.
defects.severity_rationale: Distinct valid 64-bit record IDs can collapse into one record when IDs exceed JavaScript's exact integer range.

detection_criteria.mechanism: JSON.parse turns 64-bit ids into doubles, so ids above 2^53 lose their low bits and two consecutive upstream ids become equal, making dedupeById merge different records.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the record lost, duplicated or corrupted, and the operation sequence that does it.
